mainTopic: צידה on שבת and יום טוב: when an animal counts as already trapped (enclosures, weakened or swarming creatures), and who is liable when several people trap together.
overview: This amud opens at the end of the משנה. חכמים rule that driving a deer into a garden, courtyard, or ביבר counts as trapping. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it depends on whether the animal still needs more catching (מחוסר צידה). The גמרא then contrasts a משנה in ביצה, which lets one take animals and birds from a ביבר on יום טוב, with a ברייתא that forbids it. For birds, the difference is a roofed versus an unroofed ביבר. A challenge from the house case is answered by רבה בר רב הונא: that case is about a צפור דרור, which is never controlled. Following the same method, the animal contradiction is solved by a large versus a small ביבר, and רב אשי gives tests for what counts as small. Next, שמואל rules like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and אביי teaches that learning means understanding, not just reciting. ברייתות then cover weakened deer and insects, all judged by whether the creature can still escape. The amud ends with משניות about locking a deer in a house and blocking a doorway, where only the person who completes the trapping is liable.

steps.title: חכמים: trapping a deer into a garden, courtyard, or enclosure makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The end of the חכמים's ruling in the משנה: a deer driven into a garden, courtyard, or ביבר counts as trapped, so one is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who traps a deer into a garden, a courtyard, or an enclosure is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle of the חכמים's statement. They say that chasing a deer into a garden, courtyard, or enclosure counts as the forbidden act of trapping on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the משנה, רבי יהודה said a deer is only considered trapped once it is driven into a house. The חכמים are broader: even a larger enclosed space like a garden or a ביבר is enough to make the trapping complete. This disagreement becomes the key to solving the first contradiction later on.
steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of a sentence. The speaker is the חכמים, not רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה's stricter view (deer only into a house) came on the previous amud.

phrases.english: And a deer into a garden, or into a courtyard,
phrases.notes: Continuing the חכמים's statement from the previous part of the משנה.

phrases.english: or into enclosures — he is liable.
phrases.notes: The bracketed word completes the ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה earlier (the opinion of חכמים).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Driving a deer into a garden, courtyard, or ביבר completes the act of צידה, and one is liable.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: not all enclosures are the same
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל qualifies the rule. It depends on whether the animal still needs to be chased and caught (מחוסר צידה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Not all enclosures are equal. This is the rule: if the animal still needs more catching, one is exempt. If it does not need more catching, one is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל gives a general test for when an enclosure counts as 'trapped.' If you could still not grab the animal easily, you have not trapped it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is practical: can you reach and take the animal without another chase? A big enclosure where the deer can run away is מחוסר צידה, so one is פטור. A small one where it is easily grabbed is not, so one is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who here qualifies the חכמים's rule
Still lacking trapping: the animal still needs to be chased and caught

steps.whatToRemember: The key test for trapping is מחוסר צידה: if the animal still needs another chase to be caught, the trapping is not complete.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the standard test for צידה. It explains why the same 'enclosure' can count as trapped in one case and not in another.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Not all enclosures are equal.
This is the principle:
If it still lacks trapping — he is exempt;
phrases.notes: The animal can still escape and must be chased again.

phrases.english: if it does not lack trapping — he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: לֹא כָּל הַבֵּיבָרִין שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the חכמים's blanket ruling about ביברין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for trapping depends on whether the animal is still מחוסר צידה.

steps.title: The משנה in ביצה: animals and birds may be taken from enclosures on יום טוב, fish may not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה from מסכת ביצה. Fish may not be taken from ביברין on יום טוב, but animals and birds may.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: One may not catch fish from enclosures on יום טוב, and one may not put food in front of them. But one may catch animals and birds, and one may put food in front of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a משנה from another מסכת. This sets up the first side of a contradiction that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish in a pond can still swim away, so catching them is real trapping and forbidden on יום טוב. Animals and birds in their ביבר are treated as already caught, so taking them is allowed. Food may only be given to animals that are 'ready' to be used on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned in a משנה elsewhere (here, ביצה)

phrases.english: GEMARA:
We learned there (in a mishna):

phrases.aramaic: אֵין צָדִין דָּגִים מִן הַבֵּיבָרִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not trap fish from the enclosures on a Festival,
and one may not place food before them.
But one may trap an animal or a bird,
and one may place food before them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by bringing an outside משנה about ביברין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב, animals and birds in ביברין count as already caught, but fish do not.

steps.title: A ברייתא contradicts the משנה about animals and birds
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא forbids taking animals, birds, and fish from ביברין on יום טוב. This contradicts the משנה on both animals and birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: They contradicted this: Enclosures of animals, birds, and fish — one may not catch from them on יום טוב, and one may not put food in front of them. So there is a contradiction about animals, and a contradiction about birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that forbids what the משנה allowed. It points out two separate contradictions, one about animals and one about birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said animals and birds in a ביבר are already caught. The ברייתא says they are not, since it lumps them together with fish. The fish rule matches in both sources, so only animals and birds clash.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted them: introduces a contradicting source
Animal against animal: the animal rulings clash

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּיבָרִין שֶׁל חַיּוֹת וְשֶׁל עוֹפוֹת וְשֶׁל דָּגִים —
phrases.english: Enclosures of animals, of birds, and of fish —
one may not trap from them on a Festival,
and one may not place food before them.
Animal against animal is difficult,
birds against birds is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the משנה quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה in ביצה permitting taking animals and birds from ביברין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא forbids the very same thing for animals and birds, so the two sources disagree.

steps.title: The animal contradiction is solved: רבי יהודה vs. רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The animal contradiction is not hard. The ברייתא follows רבי יהודה, and the משנה in ביצה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that animal against animal is not difficult: this one is רבי יהודה, that one is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the first contradiction by saying each source follows a different תנא from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds a deer is only trapped in a house, so in a ביבר it is not caught yet and taking it is forbidden, as the ברייתא says. The רבנן hold a ביבר is enough, so the animal is already caught and may be taken, as the משנה in ביצה says.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable / granted (sets up 'but the other part is hard')
The תנא who requires a house for a deer to be trapped
The Sages (חכמים), who accept a garden or ביבר

phrases.english: Granted, animal against animal is not difficult:
this is Rabbi Yehuda, that is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: ברייתא = רבי יהודה; משנה in ביצה = רבנן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the first half of the contradiction in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two sources to different תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seemed to give one shared view and clash.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sources reflect the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבנן about deer in enclosures.

steps.title: But the bird contradiction remains difficult
steps.stepSummary: The previous answer does not work for birds, because רבי יהודה and רבנן do not argue about birds.
steps.simpleTranslation: But birds against birds is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the second contradiction, about birds, is still unsolved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, both רבי יהודה and the רבנן agree that a bird is only trapped in a מגדל. Since they share one view on birds, we cannot split the sources between them.

phrases.english: But birds against birds is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא structure: the animal problem is solved, but the bird problem stands.
steps.kashyaTarget: The contradiction between the משנה and ברייתא regarding birds.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No מחלוקת exists about birds, so the answer from step 5 cannot apply.

steps.title: Suggested answer: a roofed vs. an unroofed enclosure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה speaks of a roofed ביבר and the ברייתא of an unroofed one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say birds against birds is also not difficult: this one is a roofed enclosure, that one is an unroofed enclosure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer for the birds ('and if you say'). This sets it up only to be rejected in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that a bird cannot fly away from a roofed enclosure, so it counts as caught, as the משנה says. In an open enclosure it can escape, so it is not caught, as the ברייתא says.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say: introduces a proposal that will be rejected

steps.confusionAlert: 'וכי תימא' signals that this answer is about to be challenged (step 8). Step 9 then defends it, so roofed vs. unroofed does end up as the answer for ordinary birds.

phrases.english: And if you say:
birds against birds is also not difficult:
this is a roofed enclosure,
phrases.notes: The משנה in ביצה, which permits.

phrases.english: that is an unroofed enclosure —

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, עוֹפוֹת אַעוֹפוֹת נָמֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a solution to the bird contradiction of step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources speak of the same kind of ביבר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed: the משנה refers to a roofed ביבר and the ברייתא to an unroofed one. Step 8 challenges this, and step 9 upholds it by limiting the house rule to a צפור דרור.

steps.title: Rejected: a house is roofed, yet a bird there is still not trapped
steps.stepSummary: Roofing cannot be the answer. Everyone agrees a bird in a house, which is roofed, is not trapped; only a מגדל counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a house is roofed, and according to both רבי יהודה and the רבנן, a bird into a closet — yes; into a house — no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the roofed-enclosure answer. The next step defends it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A house has a roof, yet our משנה says a bird driven into a house is not trapped, because it can still fly around and escape your grasp. So a roof alone does not seem to make a bird caught, and a roofed ביבר should be no different. Step 9 answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A closet or tower: a small enclosed space where a bird is easily grabbed

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבי יהודה and רבנן agree that a bird driven into a house is not trapped; only a small space like a מגדל counts. This seems to show that a roof alone is not enough. Step 9 answers this challenge.

phrases.english: But a house is roofed,
and according to both Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis,
a bird into a closet — yes (it is trapped),
into a house — no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer proposed in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Challenges the roofed vs. unroofed distinction. The challenge is answered in step 9, where רבה בר רב הונא limits the house rule to a צפור דרור and so keeps the distinction.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A house is roofed, yet all agree a bird in it is not trapped, so roofing cannot make a ביבר count as trapped.

steps.title: The משנה's bird is a free bird that cannot be controlled
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא saves the roofed/unroofed answer. The משנה that says a bird in a house is not trapped speaks of a צפור דרור, which never submits to control.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא said: Here we are dealing with a צפור דרור, because it does not accept authority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the rejection from step 8. It says the house case in the משנה is about one special kind of bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 argued that a house is roofed, yet the bird inside is not trapped, so roofing cannot be what matters. רבה בר רב הונא answers that this rule only applies to a צפור דרור, which escapes capture even indoors. For ordinary birds, a roofed ביבר does count as trapping, so the answer from step 7 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'free bird' (sparrow) that cannot be controlled

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say that birds can never be trapped indoors. Only the צפור דרור is the exception; ordinary birds in a roofed area are considered trapped.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna said:
Here we are dealing with a free bird (sparrow),
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the משנה's case of a bird in a house.

phrases.english: because it does not accept authority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the answer from step 7 against the rejection in step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A house is roofed and a bird inside is not trapped, so roofing seemed irrelevant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The house rule applies only to a צפור דרור. For other birds, a roofed ביבר means the bird is trapped.

steps.title: Why it is called a free bird
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of רבי ישמעאל supports the claim: the bird is called דרור because it lives (דרה) in a house just as freely as in a field.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Why is it called צפור דרור? Because it dwells in a house as it does in a field.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that this bird acts free even indoors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name דרור is connected to the word דרה, meaning 'dwells.' This bird behaves inside a house exactly as it does in an open field, so a house does not trap it. That is exactly what רבה בר רב הונא needs.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: As the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Why is it called a 'free bird'?
Because it dwells in a house as in a field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9
steps.raayaObject: That a צפור דרור is not controlled even inside a house
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל explaining the name

steps.title: Animals too: a large enclosure versus a small one
steps.stepSummary: Since the bird contradiction was solved by different situations, the animal contradiction can be solved the same way. The ברייתא speaks of a large ביבר, and the משנה of a small one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, the animal-against-animal contradiction is also not difficult. This one is in a large ביבר, and that one is in a small ביבר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reuses the 'different situations' method to answer the animal contradiction without a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 5), the animal contradiction was answered by saying the sources follow different תנאים. Now the גמרא says both sources can agree. In a large ביבר you still need to chase the animal, so taking it is forbidden. In a small ביבר it is already caught, so taking it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this

steps.whyThisMatters: The animal contradiction no longer depends on the dispute between רבי יהודה and the רבנן; the size of the enclosure decides it.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
animal against animal is also not difficult:
this (the baraita) is in a large enclosure,
that (the mishnah) is in a small enclosure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the method of step 9 to replace the answer from step 5
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different situations (אוקימתא) instead of a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animal sources disagree because they follow רבי יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone agrees: in a large ביבר the animal is not trapped yet, and in a small ביבר it is.

steps.title: What counts as large and what counts as small?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the definitions of a large and a small ביבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a large ביבר, and what is a small ביבר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear definition of the terms it just introduced. This sets up רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 11 only works if we know where the line falls. The גמרא needs a test for when an enclosure is small enough that the animal is already caught.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? How does it look?

phrases.english: What is a large enclosure,
and what is a small enclosure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for definitions of the terms used in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact test for a large versus a small ביבר

steps.title: רב אשי's three tests for a small enclosure
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי offers three possible tests. A ביבר is small if (1) you can catch the animal in one lunge, or (2) the walls' shadows overlap, or (3) it has no corners where the animal can hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Wherever one runs after it and reaches it in one lunge, it is a small ביבר; otherwise it is large. Or: wherever the walls' shadows fall on each other, it is small; otherwise large. Or: wherever there are no corners, it is small; otherwise large.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives three different ways to define a small ביבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three tests ask the same thing: can the animal still get away from you? If you can catch it in one lunge, or the space is narrow enough that the shadows of the walls meet, or there are no corners to dodge into, the animal is already caught. Otherwise, catching it still counts as trapping.

keyTerms.meaning: A lunge, a single bending motion

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Wherever one runs after it
and reaches it in one lunge —
it is a small enclosure;
and any other is a large enclosure.
Or alternatively: wherever
the shadow of the walls falls upon each other —
it is a small enclosure;
and any other is a large enclosure.
Or alternatively: wherever
there are no series of corners —
it is a small enclosure;
and any other is a large enclosure.

steps.whatToRemember: An animal in a small ביבר counts as already trapped, so taking it is allowed. In a large ביבר it still needs catching, so taking it is forbidden. רב אשי gives three tests for 'small.'
steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּרָהֵיט בָּתְרֵיהּ וּמָטֵי לֵהּ בְּחַד שִׁיחְיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ביבר is small if the animal can be caught in one lunge, or if the walls' shadows overlap, or if there are no corners; otherwise it is large.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. In the name of שמואל, רב יוסף rules that the הלכה follows him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, etc. רב יוסף said in the name of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה and gives a practical ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that not all enclosures are the same: it depends on whether the animal still needs catching. שמואל rules that the הלכה follows him, which sets up אביי's question.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא of the משנה; he distinguishes between kinds of enclosures

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the mishnah: not all enclosures are equal.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The halacha follows Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts discussion of the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

steps.title: אביי asks whether רבנן really disagree
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: saying 'the הלכה follows him' implies a disagreement. Do the רבנן really argue with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: 'The הלכה follows him' — does that imply that they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is arguing with the first opinion or only explaining it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You usually only say 'the הלכה follows X' when someone disagrees with X. אביי wonders whether that is true here, or whether רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is simply clarifying what everyone holds.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
'The halacha' — that implies that they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what is implied by the ruling in step 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל or whether he only explains them

steps.title: רב יוסף asks what difference it makes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף pushes back: either way the הלכה is like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so why does it matter?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What difference does it make to you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges whether אביי's question is worth asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether or not the רבנן disagree, the practical result is the same. So רב יוסף asks what is gained by looking into it.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference does it make to you?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מַאי נָפְקָא לָךְ מִינַּהּ?
phrases.english: He said to him: What difference does it make to you?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the value of אביי's question in step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The practical הלכה does not change either way, so the question seems pointless.

steps.title: Learning is not just reciting a song
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers with a saying: should we learn like someone chanting a tune? We must understand, not just memorize.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'Learn the learning, let it be a song'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends his question by explaining that understanding matters even when nothing practical changes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just memorizing rulings is like humming a song without knowing what it means. Learning the גמרא means understanding the positions, including whether there is a real disagreement.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's principle: Torah learning means understanding the reasons, not only knowing the practical bottom line.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic principle behind all Torah learning: we study even questions that have no practical difference.

phrases.english: He said to him:
'Learn the learning — let it be a song'?
phrases.notes: Rhetorical: should learning be mindless recitation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 16
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A question with no practical difference is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Understanding the סוגיא is valuable in itself.

steps.title: Trapping a blind, sleeping, lame, old, or sick deer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that trapping a blind or sleeping deer makes one liable, while trapping a lame, old, or sick deer does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One who traps a blind or sleeping deer is liable. A lame, old, or sick deer — he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about which weakened animals still count as needing to be trapped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some deer are liable to trapping and others are not. The ברייתא gives the rulings without a reason, which sets up אביי's question.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who traps a blind or sleeping deer is liable.
A lame, old, or sick deer — he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַצָּד צְבִי סוֹמֵא וְיָשֵׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: which weakened animals need trapping
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blind or sleeping deer: liable. Lame, old, or sick deer: exempt.

steps.title: אביי asks what the difference is
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף why the first group makes one liable and the second does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What is different about these, and what is different about those?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks for the reason behind the ברייתא's split. This sets up רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every animal on the list is weakened in some way. So why do a blind or sleeping deer still need trapping, but a lame, old, or sick one does not?

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי?
phrases.english: What is different about these, and what is different about those?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי, וּמַאי שְׁנָא הָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning of step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a blind or sleeping deer needs trapping but a lame, old, or sick deer does not

steps.title: Some can still run away, others cannot
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that a blind or sleeping deer will still bolt when touched. A lame, old, or sick deer cannot escape, so it counts as already trapped.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are likely to run away; those are not likely to run away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the test: can the animal still flee?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sleeping deer wakes up and a blind deer feels the touch, and both run off, so catching them is real trapping. A lame, old, or sick deer cannot escape, so it is like an animal that is already caught.

keyTerms.meaning: Likely to run away, to escape

phrases.english: These are likely to run away,
those are not likely to run away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Trapping applies only to an animal that can still escape.

steps.title: Another baraita says a sick deer makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with a different ברייתא that says trapping a sick deer makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: A sick deer — liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that two ברייתות contradict each other about a sick deer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא says one is exempt for a sick deer, but another ברייתא says liable. Both cannot be right about the same animal.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught (introducing a contradicting ברייתא)

phrases.english: But it was taught: a sick deer — liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling on a sick deer in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in step 18 that trapping a sick deer is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different ברייתא directly says the opposite about a sick deer.

steps.title: Sick with fever versus sick with exhaustion
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that there are two kinds of sickness. A deer sick with fever can still flee, so one is liable. A deer sick with exhaustion cannot flee, so one is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It is not difficult. This is a deer sick from fever; that is a deer sick from exhaustion.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the contradiction by splitting 'sick' into two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He applies רב יוסף's test, which is whether the animal can still run away. A feverish deer still has the strength to escape, so catching it is trapping and one is liable. A deer worn out by exhaustion cannot escape, so it is already caught and one is exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: The single test for all of these cases is whether the animal can still escape. If it can, catching it is trapping (liable). If it cannot, it is already trapped (exempt).

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: It is not difficult:
this one is a deer sick due to fever (liable),
that one is a deer sick due to exhaustion (exempt).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 21
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Sick' is one category, so the two ברייתות contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: A feverish deer can flee (liable); an exhausted deer cannot (exempt).

steps.title: רבי מאיר and חכמים on trapping insects
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records a dispute. רבי מאיר says trapping any of these insects makes one liable. חכמים say it depends on whether that species is normally trapped.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: One who traps locusts, cicadas, hornets, or mosquitoes on שבת is liable. That is רבי מאיר's view. חכמים say: if the species is normally trapped, he is liable. If the species is not normally trapped, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about trapping insects on שבת. It records a disagreement between רבי מאיר and חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר treats all these insects as trappable, so trapping any of them is a full צידה. חכמים add a condition: the act only counts as צידה if people normally trap that kind of creature. If nobody normally traps it, catching it is not the מלאכה of צידה.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. This introduces a ברייתא.

steps.whyThisMatters: The view of חכמים sets a basic rule: whether something counts as צידה depends on whether that species is normally hunted. This idea comes up again across הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who traps locusts, cicadas,
hornets, or mosquitoes on Shabbat
is liable. These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
Any creature whose species is normally trapped: he is liable.
And any creature whose species is not normally trapped: he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from trapping deer in different conditions to trapping insects.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, trapping any of these insects makes one liable. According to חכמים, one is liable only if that species is normally trapped.

steps.title: Locusts in the dew versus in the heat
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says trapping locusts in the cool dew is exempt and in the heat is liable. אלעזר בן מהבאי adds that if they are swarming, one is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: One who traps locusts when there is dew is exempt. When it is hot, he is liable. אלעזר בן מהבאי says: if they were swarming in, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about locusts, where the ruling depends on the weather. אלעזר בן מהבאי then adds a case where the locusts are swarming.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the cool dew, locusts are sluggish and cannot fly away, so they already count as caught. This matches the rule from the deer that are too weak to escape. In the heat they are lively, so catching them is real צידה. אלעזר בן מהבאי says swarming locusts are so easy to grab that taking them is not trapping, but he does not say which time of day he means.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא
At the time of dew, when it is cool and the locusts are sluggish
At the time of heat, when the locusts are lively
Streaming or swarming in, flowing in great numbers

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
One who traps locusts at the time of dew is exempt;
at the time of heat, he is liable.
Elazar ben Mehavai says:
If they were swarming in, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ: הַצָּד חֲגָבִים בִּשְׁעַת הַטַּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of insects, now focusing on how the condition of the locusts changes the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trapping locusts in the dew is exempt and in the heat is liable. אלעזר בן מהבאי exempts one who takes swarming locusts.

steps.title: Which case does אלעזר בן מהבאי refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether אלעזר בן מהבאי's comment about swarming goes on the first case (dew) or the second case (heat).
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is אלעזר בן מהבאי referring to the first case or to the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about how to read the ברייתא it just quoted. It is setting up a source that will answer it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he refers to the first case (the רישא), he is being stricter: even in the dew one is liable unless the locusts are swarming. If he refers to the last case (the סיפא), he is being more lenient: even in the heat, swarming locusts are exempt. The words of the ברייתא can be read either way.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them
It stands on, it refers to

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge against anyone. It is a real reading question: we know what אלעזר בן מהבאי said, but not which case he was talking about.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is Elazar ben Mehavai referring to the first clause,
or is he referring to the last clause?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to understand the comment of אלעזר בן מהבאי from the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the swarming exemption change the dew case (making it stricter) or the heat case (making it more lenient)?

steps.title: Swarming exempts even in the heat
steps.stepSummary: Another version of the ברייתא says outright: "even at the time of heat," swarming locusts are exempt. So the comment refers to the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who traps locusts in the dew is exempt, and in the heat is liable. אלעזר בן מהבאי says: even in the heat, if they were swarming, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a version of the ברייתא that spells out what אלעזר בן מהבאי meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added word "even" (אפילו) settles it. אלעזר בן מהבאי is talking about the heat case and giving a leniency. Even lively locusts do not need real trapping when they swarm in so heavily that one can simply scoop them up.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear. This introduces a proof or an answer.

steps.whatToRemember: Locusts in the dew are already as good as caught, so one is exempt. Locusts in the heat require real צידה, so one is liable. Even in the heat, swarming locusts are exempt, because grabbing them takes no trapping effort.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who traps locusts at the time of dew is exempt;
at the time of heat, he is liable.
Elazar ben Mehavai says:
Even at the time of heat,
if they were swarming in, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הַצָּד חֲגָבִין בִּשְׁעַת הַטַּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He refers to the סיפא. Even in the heat, swarming locusts are exempt.

steps.title: משנה: locking a deer inside a house
steps.stepSummary: If one person locks a door in front of a deer, he is liable. If two lock it together, they are exempt. If one person could not have locked it alone and two did, they are liable. רבי שמעון exempts them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a deer entered a house and one person locked the door in front of it, he is liable. If two people locked it, they are exempt. If one person could not lock it alone and two people locked it, they are liable. רבי שמעון exempts them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It covers trapping a deer by locking it inside a house, and what happens when two people do the locking together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Locking the door counts as trapping, because the deer is now confined. When two people do a job that one could have done alone, neither did a full מלאכה, so both are exempt. When the job needs two people, that is the normal way to do it, so both are liable. רבי שמעון holds that two people sharing one מלאכה are never liable.

keyTerms.meaning: And he locked the door in front of it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a key source for the rule of שנים שעשאוה, meaning two people who perform one מלאכה together.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A deer that entered a house
and one person locked the door in front of it: he is liable.
If two people locked it, they are exempt.
If one person was unable to lock it
and two people locked it, they are liable.
And Rabbi Shimon exempts them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. The insect discussion is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One person locking the door is liable. Two people doing what one could do are exempt. Two people doing what one could not do are liable, but רבי שמעון exempts them.

steps.title: שמואל: a lion is trapped only in its cage
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that trapping a lion makes one liable only once it is brought into its cage.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of שמואל: One who traps a lion on שבת is not liable until he brings it into its cage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא on this משנה brings שמואל's rule that a lion is not considered trapped until it is inside its cage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that locking a deer in a house is trapping. שמואל explains that for a lion, locking it inside a house is not enough. A lion is so dangerous and strong that it is only truly under control in its own cage.

keyTerms.meaning: Cage, a special enclosure for a lion

steps.confusionAlert: A lion is still a creature that can be trapped. Only the point at which trapping is complete is different for it.

phrases.english: GEMARA:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said that Shmuel said:
One who traps a lion on Shabbat is not liable
until he brings it into its cage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the משנה's rule that locking an animal in a house counts as trapping.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Trapping a lion is complete only once it is in its cage.

steps.title: משנה: the second person completes the blocking of the doorway
steps.stepSummary: If the first person sat in the doorway without filling it and a second person sat and filled it, the second person is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If one person sat in the doorway and did not fill it, and a second person sat and filled it, the second person is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה describes trapping a deer by sitting in a doorway. In this first case, the second person is the one who completes the trapping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the first person sits there without filling the doorway, the deer can still get out, so nothing has been trapped yet. The second person's sitting is what closes the gap and finishes the צידה. That is why he is the one who is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: He filled it, meaning he blocked it completely

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If one person sat in the doorway
and did not fill it,
and the second person sat and filled it,
the second person is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about trapping by blocking a doorway with one's body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The person who completes the blocking of the doorway is the one who is liable.

steps.title: משנה: the first person already trapped the deer
steps.stepSummary: If the first person already filled the doorway, he is liable. A second person who sits next to him is exempt, even after the first person leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first person sat in the doorway and filled it, and a second person came and sat beside him, then even if the first person later got up and left, the first person is liable and the second is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case. Here the first person finishes the trapping completely on his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the first person fills the doorway, the deer is already trapped. The second person adds nothing new. Even when the first person leaves, the second is only keeping a deer that was already trapped, not trapping it.

keyTerms.meaning: The first is liable and the second is exempt

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the second person becomes liable when the first one leaves. Trapping is a single act, and the first person already finished it.

phrases.english: If the first person sat in the doorway and filled it,
and the second person came and sat beside him,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁעָמַד הָרִאשׁוֹן וְהָלַךְ לוֹ
phrases.english: even though the first person stood up and went away,
the first person is liable and the second is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite case to step 29. Here the first person finishes the trapping alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first person, who filled the doorway, is liable. The second person, who only sat beside him, is exempt even after the first person leaves.

steps.title: The comparison: locking a house with a deer already inside
steps.stepSummary: The משנה compares the second person to someone who locks his house for security and happens to keep an already-trapped deer inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this like? It is like someone who locks his house to guard it, and it turns out a deer is kept inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a comparison that explains why the second person is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Locking a house that already has a trapped deer inside only guards something that is already caught. Making a trapped animal more secure is not the act of צידה. The second person in the doorway is doing the same thing, so he is exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: צידה happens only once, at the moment the animal first becomes trapped. The person who completes that moment is liable. Anyone who only guards an animal that is already trapped is exempt.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule for צידה: making an already-trapped animal more secure is not a new act of trapping.

phrases.english: To what is this similar?
To one who locks his house to guard it
and it turns out a deer is kept secured inside it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the second person in step 30 is exempt.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Making an already-trapped animal more secure is not צידה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second person only guards a deer that is already trapped, so he is exempt.
